summary: Feed s169_triple is degraded: NDR missing bidirectional visibility (34.1% one-way sessions), receiving 17.9% duplicates, and 10.2% truncated frames to 192B despite needing full payload.

findings.root_cause: Overlapping SPAN/TAP sources or both sides of a link fed to broker without deduplication - same packets arriving via two paths, resulting in 478 of 2667 packets (17.9%) duplicated.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes 10G port bandwidth and processing on duplicates, inflates flow/session counts, skews baselines and can hide true anomalies.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short window so NDR sees each packet once and analytics are accurate.

findings.root_cause: Both directions of TCP sessions not aggregated to same tool port - likely asymmetric routing with separate SPANs or hash-based load-balancing splitting client->server and server->client to different outputs. 57 of 167 sessions (34.1%) are one-way.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions for TCP reassembly and stateful detection; one-way traffic breaks session reconstruction, causing missed intrusions, broken flow records and false positives.

recommended_fix.why: Configure broker flow-aware aggregation to send both directions of each session to this NDR port to restore complete session visibility.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing enabled cutting frames to ~192 bytes (272 of 2667 frames, 10.2% truncated), likely default snaplen to save bandwidth.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep packet inspection; truncated packets lose L7 content so signatures, malware and protocol detection fail on affected traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing / set snaplen to 9216 (tool max) so NDR receives full packets for complete payload analysis.
